items.title: 'Grossly inadequate': NT traditional owners plan to mandate mine rehabilitation

children.content: Traditional owners in the NT want to see more money put aside for the rehabilitation of closed mines and are considering making it a requirement of any agreement established between mine companies and traditional owners.

image.altText: A haul truck is being loaded with iron ore in the open-pit of Roper Bar mine in the NT.

items.title: Fierce division over highly flammable grass pastoralists rely on

children.content: Buffel grass is thriving and spreading across South Australia, increasing the risk of bushfires. But not everyone agrees on how to manage it.

image.altText: A man in hi-vis clothing sprays chemical onto buffel grass.

children.content: Acclaimed Alice Springs filmmaker Warwick Thornton is also a diehard rev head and amateur mechanic who loves old cars — and he's making his Red CentreNATS debut this year with a lovingly restored 1970s Toyota FJ 40 "bull chaser".

items.title: Darwin hospital opens new ward with hopes of easing capacity pressures

children.content: A new multi-purpose ward at the Northern Territory's largest hospital has received its first patients this week, with hopes the $24 million investment will help ease capacity pressures in Darwin's health sector.

image.altText: A patient resting in a hospital bed, a health worker is standing next to her and looking at a health monitoring screen nearby.

items.title: Tourists survive 'scary' buffalo attack on popular NT hiking trail

children.content: Two young tourists say they've never been more scared in their lives after 21-year-old Victorian woman Emma Hipwell was charged by a wild buffalo while holidaying in the Northern Territory.

image.altText: Emma Hipwell lifts her shorts to show a number of large bruises on her right hip.

items.title: 'No-one told us anything': NT community without services months after floods

children.content: Months after record flooding, the remote Aboriginal community of Nauiyu / Daly River remains significantly damaged and without key services. Locals say some are still without power and little has been done to prepare for the next wet season.

image.altText: A group of white roof homes right on the bank of a large green river, with trees surrounding it.

items.title: Dugong population drops 50pc in 'real shock' for researchers

children.content: The number of dugongs in the Gulf of Carpentaria, one of the animal's most globally important populations, has halved in the past two decades, a decline scientists have called a "real shock".

image.altText: a dugong in water

items.title: Hegseth thanks Australia for 'matched' defence capabilities

children.content: US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth thanks Australia for its ongoing friendship and the need to "ensure our capabilities match and are complementary". Follow live.

image.altText: Richard Marles and Pete Hegseth smile outside the Pentagon with miltary members forming an honour cordon.

items.title: Coalition unveils plan to slash tobacco tax by $24 a pack

children.content: A future Coalition government would slash the tobacco excise by 80 per cent, legalise and tax vapes and nicotine pouches, and bolster law enforcement to shut down the illicit trade.

image.altText: Angus Taylor at a press conference.

items.title: Australia facing a 'looming crisis' as people enter retirement as lifelong renters

children.content: More people are edging towards retirement as "forever renters". They are making tough decisions about work, where to live and how they will afford to retire.

children.content: A survey of about 400 teachers finds classroom disruption has a significant negative effect on the health of teachers, with female teachers the most affected.

image.altText: A boy writes with a pencil in a classroom.

children.content: Emergency crews have contained a fire at Tungatinah Power Station and an investigation is set to be launched.

items.title: Record warm winter brings disappointing end to snow season

children.content: An unseasonably warm and wet June brought a challenging start to the 2026 snow season and while a snow base came by July over the higher slopes, the lower alpine regions missed out on full coverage.

image.altText: Skiers on a snowfield in Perisher.

items.title: Sydney gangland war's disturbing crossfire casualties trend continues

children.content: Bungled assassinations and death by association have become more frequent in Sydney's underworld war as a potential sixth innocent victim is killed in the past 18 months.

items.title: Brown and foul tasting: This town's water may be the tipping point of a crisis
